thread:
ana: Heads up — after the kernel-selector rollout at 02:15 UTC we saw a 16% absolute drop in prefix cache hit-rate for v2 models (88% -> 72%). Not huge but correlates with a latency tail increase.
mike: ack. Do we have a profiler trace?
ana: yes attached a sampling profile from host-a1 around the spike, main points: more short-prefix requests are missing cache and hitting the slower path, and KV load amplification is up ~2.3x.
sofie: could this be key canonicalization? We changed a thing in kernel selector that reorders toolcall args for affinity grouping last week.
devon: right — kernel selection PR also introduced a batching alignment layer that pre-trims trailing whitespace in prompt headers for batching efficiency. That might affect cache keys if normalization differs.
perf-bot: perf alert: model=v2, metric=prefix_cache_hit_rate, baseline=0.88, current=0.72, delta=-0.16, p95_latency_delta=+28ms.
ryan: Do we have examples of cache keys before/after? A few request payloads would help.
ana: pasted two sample requests (sanitized). Note the tool call json ordering change in request B.
ana: Request A: {"prompt":"Summarize: ...","system":"<base>","tools":[{"name":"search","q":"x"},{"name":"format","opts":{"style":"short"}}]}
ana: Request B (post-change): {"prompt":"Summarize: ... ","system":"<base>\n","tools":[{"name":"format","opts":{"style":"short"}},{"name":"search","q":"x"}]}
mike: I see the trailing space and the swapped tools order. If our cache key pipeline includes raw prompt + system + tools serial form, both changes will create distinct keys.
sofie: We intentionally do minimal normalization upstream because we worry about semantic changes. But small policy diffs (e.g., trimming) should probably not be cache-key breaking.
devon: Proposal: make cache key include a canonicalized prompt signature: (tokenizer_version, normalized_prompt, sorted_tool_signatures, system_hash). That should be stable across non-semantic reorders.
ana: quick prototype for normalization I used in the profiler run:```python
def canonical_prompt(req):
    toks = tokenize(req['prompt'])
    # include tokenizer fingerprint
    tv = tokenizer.version
    system = req.get('system','').strip()  # intentionally trim
    tools = req.get('tools',[])
    tool_sigs = [ (t['name'], signature_of(t.get('opts',{}))) for t in tools ]
    tool_sigs.sort()  # deterministic order
    return f"v{tv}:{system}:{hash_tuple(toks,tool_sigs)}"
```
ryan: Sorting tool sigs is okay, but mind that some callables rely on order for semantics. We should only sort by tool identity+opts if tools are declared as unordered in the schema.
sofie: True — we need to consult the tool contract. For many internal tools order doesn't matter, but for some pipelines it does.
mike: Another angle: add a tokenizer_version bit to the key so we don't mix tokens when tokenizer upgrades happen. We already saw small hit-rate drops during tokenizers bumps.
ana: profiler shows ~40% of the misses correspond to requests where tokenizer_version in header was missing (client fallback) — so we were accidentally mixing variants.
devon: Fix: require client to send tokenizer_version or infer via pinned model metadata and include that in key. Quick patch for server to reject unspecified with a warning; ops can track.
ops-bot: deployment note: rolling patch queued to staging (canary=3 hosts) to include tokenizer_version enforcement and tool_sig sorting (only for tools flagged unordered).
ryan: For warmup strategy: I think we should proactively prefill the prefix cache for the top 500 prefixes per model during deploy. That would mask transient regressions while we roll fixes.
sofie: Agreed. Also add a temporary fallback policy in the kernel selector: if cache-hit-rate for small prefixes (<16 tokens) falls below 80% route those requests to the legacy kernel path that preserves the old normalization semantics.
mike: How will we measure success? Suggested metrics: prefix_cache_hit_rate (by model, token-length bucket), kv_load_per_request, p95_generation_latency, and rollout-error-rate.
ana: Created a small dashboard query: "select model, len(prompt_tokens) as L, avg(cache_hit::int) from prefix_hits where ts > now()-1h group by model, L" — will post link.
devon: Quick A/B plan: canary hosts apply key-change+tokenizer enforcement. Compare hits vs control across 30m windows. If _improvement_ not seen, revert selectively.
ryan: Edgecases: system prompt mutations — some clients append ephemeral session metadata to system. We should either strip known ephemeral markers or hash system after canonicalizing keys.
sofie: Also flag: tool opts with unordered dicts can nondeterministically serialize. We need a serializer that sorts object keys and normalizes numbers vs strings.
ana: I ran a small offline replay: normalizing tool opts (sort keys + stable float repr) recovered ~8% of the hit-rate loss on the sample corpus. Good sign.
mike: Timeline? Can we get a staging patch today and a controlled canary tomorrow morning?
devon: I'll open a PR with three changes: (1) tokenizer_version required header + key bit, (2) sorted-tool-sigs for unordered tools, (3) legacy-route fallback for short prefixes. Requesting reviewer: @sofie @ana.
sofie: Review ack. Also add a unit test for cache-key invariance on whitespace-only system diffs.
ana: Ops notes: warmup job to backfill top prefixes scheduled for 03:30 UTC. ops-bot will post status in thread.
ops-bot: warmup job started on canary hosts (3), target prefixes=500/model, estimated runtime=6m.
perf-bot: quick update: after warmup the canary hosts show local hit-rate +6pp and p95 down 12ms. Still below baseline but trending.
ryan: good. Keep an eye on kv amplification. If it stays high we should consider more aggressive in-memory caching tiers.
mike: thanks team — let's track in the runbook under the incident id `prefetch-5199`. Small action items: devon PR, ops warmup, dashboard link, unit tests.
ana: I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft once we have canary A/B data. :+1:
devon: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/8421 (wip)
sofie: reading PR now.

perf-bot: canary aggregate: hit_rate=0.78, control=0.72, p95_delta=-10ms. Continuing monitoring for 2h.

mike: nice work.
sofie: moving to review/merge after test green.
